title: Add a new how operation without changing what content
hypothesis: A compact operation-only Mirror code inferred from support examples will add an aligned new transform over frozen content without modifying content state or storing a full operator, while unrelated dynamics reveal a private-state boundary.
physical_object: frozen 8-dimensional content representation and old operation bank
mirror_coordinate: four Givens angles for a new operation, inferred from support input/output pairs
logical_multiplicity: three old operations plus one new operation acting on existing content

selection.method: secrets.randbelow over sorted eligible P0/UNTESTED IDs after exclusions

development.purpose: validate operation fit and heldout metric only; no fresh tuning

paid_objects: new operation code or fitted matrix

success_gate: For aligned new operation at support=8, all 3 fresh worlds have held-out normalized MSE <=1e-5, payload <=0.90x full operator, and old-operation retention MSE <=1e-5. Unrelated full-operator diagnostic must fit with normalized MSE <=1e-5 while compact structured codes fail above 0.1.
mirror_specific_gate: Mirror must beat the ordinary structured operation embedding by >=10% payload or a predeclared quality improvement at matched bytes; the direct embedding uses the same operation code and transform family.
failure_gate: Aligned quality/retention/storage gate misses, or ordinary operation-code control matches Mirror within 10% bytes at matched quality.
boundaries: Synthetic linear transform task only; no learned RNN or neural content encoder.
New operation angle codes are fit from support examples, not supplied directly.
Mirror and ordinary structured null control share the same serialized function state; byte/hash/quality identity is a planned falsification control.
Unrelated dense transform is a private-state diagnostic.
No task-combination count is interpreted as independent capacity.
